numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For very small K (e.g. K = 1e-11), exponnorm(K).cdf([-4, 4]) returns [-9.99968e-01, -3.16712e-05], i.e. negative CDF values; the printed exponnorm values are the negatives of the normal values. The log pdf also becomes unstable (sudden decrease of predicted log pdf for K approaching values smaller than 1e-8). Cancellation occurs in logpdf, cdf and sf for small K.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: exponnorm(K).cdf([-4, 4]) should approach the standard normal CDF, [3.16712e-05, 9.99968e-01] for K = 1e-11, with logpdf, cdf and sf stable and approaching the standard normal as K -> 0.
trigger_conditions: very small shape parameter K, e.g. K = 1e-11 (issue reproducer), with K <~ 1e-9 described as the failing range
K below 1e-6 in the original unit tests coverage gap
evaluation at large erfc arguments (large u = (-x + 1/K)/sqrt(2)), where erfc cancellation occurs
fix uses erfcx branch when K < 1 and u >= 0; otherwise the default branch
oracle_clues: issue reproducer prints normal cdf vs exponnorm cdf at x = [-4, 4] for K = 1e-11
PR tests verify correct behavior at K = 1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15 by comparing against the standard normal distribution
mpmath high-precision reference implementation used in PR discussion (mp_exponnorm_logpdf, mp.dps = 75) with relative error comparisons
assert np.all(np.isfinite(rerr)) in reference comparison script

numerical_characteristics.precision: 64-bit (float64); the reference mpmath computations use mp.dps = 75 high precision
numerical_characteristics.magnitude: very small shape parameter K (K <~ 1e-9 in the original PR, threshold revised to K < 1; tests at K = 1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15; discussion notes convergence to standard normal for K below about 1e-14 is indistinguishable in float64); arguments x spanning roughly [-1e10, 1e10] in the logpdf reproducer and [-1e30, 1e30] in the later error study
numerical_characteristics.tolerance: rtol=5e-13 is used in the existing test_sf_small_K; the new test uses assert_allclose default tolerances; relative errors are only computed where reference magnitude exceeds 1e-16, absolute error where reference is below 1e16; no explicit pass/fail threshold separating correct from incorrect answers is stated
category_specific_evidence: Issue gh-24551 reproducer: exponnorm(K=1e-11).cdf at x=[-4,4] compared against norm.cdf, showing the cancellation in exponnorm.cdf.
PR 24597 fixes cancellation in exponnorm.logpdf, exponnorm.cdf and exponnorm.sf using erfcx-based branching for small K.
Commit message: branch used only for K < 1e-6 and u >= 0 initially; later revised to K < 1 based on numerical analysis.

Discussion: the relative error study over k = logspace(-20, 0) showed errors persisting for K < 1e-18 before the fix, and after adjusting threshold to K < 1 errors were examined with mpmath reference.
Maintainer comment: cancellation reduces accuracy of the existing implementation for essentially all K < 1, not only very small K.
New test test_extremely_small_K parametrized over K in [1e-9, 1e-12, 1e-15] checks logpdf, cdf and sf against the standard normal at x in [-10.5, -3, -1, 1, 3, 10.5].
Maintainer requested changes only to _cdf, _sf and _logpdf, with existing methods renamed (e.g. _logpdf_nonnegative_u) and new methods choosing between negative and non-negative u cases.
reproduction_risks: The float64 result for K below about 1e-14 is essentially indistinguishable from the normal distribution, so reproduction must compare against the normal reference, not a fixed expected value.
The reference mpmath computations require high precision (mp.dps = 75); a float64 reference would not be trustworthy.
The K threshold changed during review (1e-6 to 1), so the expected behavior depends on which revision is reproduced.
Sampling of K and x ranges strongly affects the measured maximum relative error.
